Voting is underway across the United States in the 2026 midterm elections, with control of Congress at stake. All 435 seats in the U.S. House of Representatives, 35 Senate seats and 36 governorships are contested, and more than 57 million ballots were cast early before Election Day.

The U.S. Department of Justice said it would send 1,000 election monitors to cities and counties in all 50 states on November 3, which it called the largest monitoring effort in its history. Tens of thousands of grassroots activists organized by nonpartisan and partisan groups are also monitoring polling places, according to USA TODAY's live Election Day coverage.

In Texas, polls are open from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time, and voters in line by 7 p.m. can still cast a ballot. Voters can confirm their registration and polling place at VoteTexas.gov.

What it means for readers here

For Webb County, the national stakes arrive on the same ballot as the local ones. Voters here are deciding the TX-28 House seat and a U.S. Senate seat alongside Laredo's mayor, four City Council seats, a municipal judge and the non-binding Proposition 1 question on expanded pediatric hospital services. Whoever wins those federal races will represent this border region in Washington for the final two years of the current presidential term — on trade, border policy and federal funding questions that land directly in Laredo.

Results will come in through the evening as polls close state by state. Close races may take longer to call, and official results are certified by state and local election authorities after Election Day.
